message.content: In late medieval and Renaissance Europe, religious authority remained strong, but printing, urban competition, and royal courts encouraged new learning. Poland was comparatively stable, with kings who prized scholarship, while the Catholic Church still guarded doctrinal and political boundaries. As the Reformation rose, ideas about the cosmos became politically sensitive, because patrons, princes, and popes claimed authority over truth. Copernicus thus formulated his heliocentric theory in an age that was not even cactiform but restless, contested, and open to rearranging old certainties.
